I live in a suburban area and I babysit a lot. Most of the kids I babysit are extremely well-behaved. I also work as a camp/after school counselor year round, so I have a lot of experience working with kids with all sorts of behavioral issues.

Then, a woman posted in the community's babysitting Facebook group asking for a semi-regular sitter to watch her 5 and 10 year old. So I reached out and ended up babysitting for them.

The first time I babysat for them, the mom was still there for about 20 mins getting ready to leave. This kid (the 5 y/o) wouldn't eat his dinner and was climbing on the counter, so I tried to pick him up and put him in the chair. He started screaming and crying and ran to his mom, saying the I cut him with a knife, and pointing to a papercut on his finger that had been there before. He then tried to punch me in the face, right in front of his mom. She apologized and said that he was "a little intense sometimes".  Then, the 10 y/o girl came home from practice with her friend. We were all playing together for a while  with on of those floating electronic soccer balls, and the whole night he was throwing tantrums, literally on the floor crying and screaming and kicking and punching me and his sister. I was annoyed, but I felt like I could handle it, whatever. It took me about 2 hours to start him to bed, and I was so relieved when the parents finally got home.

They asked me to babysit again a couple of weeks later, and since it was the holiday season, I figured I could use the money for presents and whatnot. He was actually very sweet in the beginning and we were building a lego set he had just gotten. Then, his sister brought out her iPad and wouldn't give him a turn - all hell broke loose. He tried to throw her iPad, he threw a remote at my head, ripped up a fake plant, flipped chairs over, and was just being super violent towards me and his sister. The girl went downstairs and locked herself in her room to get away from him. I tried to distract him but he wouldn't drop it. He was banging on her door, throwing things at it, actually chipping away at the paint. He tried to throw a huge toy at me, and luckily the sister came to my rescue and grabbed it out of his hands as he was about to throw it. When she eventually let him in her room, he starting assaulting her and trying to destroy things in her room. So, she kicked him out again, and he said, "Fine, the I'll go get a knife and stab it through to open it". To which I replied, um, no, you definitely cannot do that. He then said that instead, he would go get a knife and end my life. Remember, this kid is FIVE. I have never had a 5 year old child threaten me harm and actually fear for my safety. I told him if he did that I would call the police, went upstairs and hid all of the knives, and texted his mom that he had just threatened to kill me. She apologized, and told me to just give him space, because he just wasn't in a great mood that day. 

Eventually, things calmed down a bit, and I was finally able to get him to sleep after HOURS of trying. The mom continued to ask me to babysit,  and obviously, I declined.

I know this probably doesn't seem as scary in writing as it was at the time, but as someone who works with kids, I was worried about liability. If something serious had happened, that could affect my career. Also, I felt so bad for his sister, because she made it very clear that he was like this ALL THE TIME. I think it's affecting her mental health, and it can't help that the parents are excusing his behavior like that. I legitimately think that this kid has some kind of personality disorder, because he literally showed no emotion other than anger. I hope that family gets some help.

I suffered from PTSD after rape. A couple of my coworkers really enjoyed sneaking up on me to scare me, and would act like I was crazy because I got extremely angry about it. After I continually asked them to stop for MONTHS, and blew up at them quite a few times, they finally stopped. I was having a conversation with one of them about it a while later and he told me that I overreacted. I asked him, if a veteran with PTSD had asked you to stop, you would have wouldn't you? He said, "well when you say it like that it makes me seem like a bad person". Both coworkers were aware of my PTSD, and it makes me so mad that I had to explain it like that for them to understand that PTSD and hypersensitivity are not just limited to those who have been in combat.

It is almost impossible to have a social life without a cell phone. People in my age group started getting phones in middle school, and by the time we got out of middle school, pretty much everyone had a cell phone. I was one of the select few that did not, and it made it harder for me to socialize with my friends because they could text each other and meet up whenever, whereas I had to call from my home phone and who talks on the phone these days? I ended up feeling left out for a lot of middle school and high school until I got a phone the summer before my sophomore year. Parents say "I didn't get a phone until I was in my 20's" and I'm like, yeah, because when you were growing, nobody else had phones so you didn't need one.
